description: P3 consumer-assertion + live-constant pin for CHECK 14 (no turn-terminating language in sub-step skill body prose, issue #321). A skill body loads into its CALLING AGENT's context, so caller-scoped terminal prose makes an agent that invokes the skill inline end its turn early and return the skill's output as its own — a silent false PASS. CHECK 14 runs TWO passes with TWO DIFFERENT invariants, so it takes ONE CORPUS PER PASS, never one corpus shared by both. Caller discovery reads `emit_body_lines` (frontmatter, fenced blocks and table rows EXCLUDED — its invariant is `a line that really invokes a sub-step`, and those regions do not invoke anything). The skill-body scan reads `emit_all_lines` (ZERO structural exclusions — its invariant is `text that loads into the calling agent's context`, and a Skill-tool invocation loads the WHOLE file, so a terminal phrase inside frontmatter, a fenced block, or a table row is read and obeyed exactly like body prose). Sharing one emitter across both passes was this check's FIFTH defect: the exclusions correct for discovery let a table row and a fenced block carry a banned phrase past the scan untouched. Three consumers pin the split at its load-bearing points: the skill-body scan's ACTUAL loop feed (`done < <(emit_all_lines "$substep_file")`), so reverting the scan to the exclusion-bearing emitter fails; the caller-discovery feed (`done < <(emit_body_lines "$agent_file"`), so collapsing the two in the other direction fails; and `emit_all_lines() {` as its own function definition, so the exclusion-free emitter cannot be quietly inlined away. KNOWN LIMITATION, stated rather than worked around: consumers are PRESENCE-only substring checks and `absent: true` scopes to YAML frontmatter, so the NON-presence of the old feed inside a shell script cannot be asserted; binding each pass's real loop-feed source is the strongest available guard, and is strictly stronger than pinning a mere mention of the emitter name. Widening the scan to the whole file also brings frontmatter newly IN SCOPE, which makes the KEEP phrase load-bearing for real content: `detect-remediation-signals` line 4 reads `..., and stop-and-merge signals ...` inside its description, whose literal `and stop` matches the terminal regex — only the `stop-and-merge` KEEP strip keeps that legitimate domain term from being reported. The set_check pins the DETECTION CONSTANTS AS THEY LIVE IN tools/policy_check.sh: it captures the single-quoted RHS body of every line-anchored CHECK14_(TERMINAL|KEEP|TOKEN)_REGEX assignment in the check itself and asserts set EQUALITY, not membership. Equality is what closes the class: a MISSING member fails (deleting a terminal alternative, dropping the `^Emit exactly` anchor, weakening the `stop-and-merge` KEEP phrase, or loosening the token regex's namespace/charset), and an EXTRA member fails too (a shadowing later reassignment that leaves the pinned assignment as dead text can no longer smuggle a weakened live value past the pin). It pins the three live regex constants only — it does not assert the check's runtime behaviour on any sample body, and the non-regex CHECK14_SKILLTOOL_MARKER is pinned by full-literal consumer instead. Because the terminal regex carries NO capitalization alternatives, the case-insensitivity that makes `Final action is a Bash tool call` and `final action is a ...` ONE detected class lives in the grep INVOCATION, so both invocation sites are pinned as consumers (`grep -qiE` detect + `grep -oiE` extract): dropping either `-i` silently reopens the capitalized-variant evasion while the pinned regex body still matches, and the extract flag must track the detect flag or a capitalized hit reports an empty phrase. The consumers pin the load-bearing literals proving the check exists and keeps its contract: the `=== CHECK 14:` section header, `add_finding 'CHECK14'` (it emits CHECK14 findings), the caller-derived discovery that excludes overlord.md, the two position-free discovery constants (Skill-tool marker literal, token regex assignment name), the two case-insensitive terminal-match invocations, and the three fail-closed findings — empty derived set, marked-but-unresolvable line, and mention/token parity failure.

expected_set: Your final action|final action is a|produce zero (text|chat)|^Emit exactly|and stop
